author: feral-core
description: FERAL's escape hatch for tasks no other skill covers: writes ad-hoc Python/Node/bash scripts to the user's ~/.feral/workspace/scripts/ folder, executes them in the Docker sandbox, and keeps a reusable catalog. The Docker sandbox is MANDATORY and there is no fallback: SkillExecutor refuses every endpoint of this skill with HTTP 503 when Docker is not installed or not healthy, which is the default on macOS, and that refusal covers list_catalog and delete too even though they run no code. Before offering this skill, confirm Docker is running; when it is not, say so and use coding_tools__bash inside a granted folder instead of promising a script. Use this whenever no existing skill fits the user's request, you can still deliver the result by generating a tiny script on the fly. A persistent workspace-scoped exec with reuse.

endpoints.description: Write code to ~/.feral/workspace/scripts/<uuid>.<ext> and execute it in the Docker sandbox. Refused with HTTP 503 when the Docker sandbox is unavailable; there is no host execution path for this endpoint. Supports language in {python, bash, node}. Persistent, the script stays for reuse. On success, a catalog entry is recorded so future turns can reference it by name. Use this when no specialized skill fits but the task is expressible as a short program.

params.name: code
params.description: Complete source code. For python, print() your answer. For bash/node, echo / console.log.

params.name: name
params.description: Short human-friendly name for the catalog (e.g. 'csv_to_json'). Auto-generated if omitted.

params.name: args
params.description: Optional stringified JSON args forwarded to the script as env var FERAL_ARGS.

endpoints.description: List previously-saved scripts that succeeded. This reads a JSON file and runs no code, so it works whether or not the Docker sandbox is available. Each entry has id, name, language, path, args_schema (if provided). Use this before writing a new script, a previous one may already do the job.
endpoints.returns_description: {scripts: [{id, name, language, path, created_at, last_run, runs}]}

endpoints.description: Re-run a previously-saved script by id, optionally overriding args. Refused with HTTP 503 when the Docker sandbox is unavailable.

params.name: args
params.description: Optional stringified JSON args forwarded as FERAL_ARGS.

endpoints.description: Delete a saved script and its catalog entry. Runs no code, so it works whether or not the Docker sandbox is available.

params.name: script_id
params.description: Catalog id of the script to delete.
